precepts.text: The rest of the acts of Rehoboam, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? There is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Judah. We do not have that book.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 14 the Lord had Ezra write the books over: “In forty days they wrote two hundred and four books.” The first were to be published openly, “that the worthy and unworthy may read it”, but the seventy last were kept back. The scriptures themselves show that this is true, because they name books we do not have.

Joshua 10:13 is the first: “Is not this written in the book of Jasher?” There is a book of Jasher, part of the Bible, one of the books Ezra wrote over, and we don't have it today.

Then 1 Kings: “Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Judah. Guess what? We don't have that book.

Rehoboam's acts were written down in full, and the Bible sends you to that book for the rest of them. The book is named, but it is not in our hands. It is another witness that more was written than what we hold today.

precepts.text: The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. We do not have that today either.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
The southern kingdom had its chronicles, and so did the northern: “And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Israel, and we don't have that today either.

The book of Jasher is missing the same way. Is it that book of Jasher they have out there on the Bible apps? No. Those of y'all that have Bible apps, leave that book alone. It is said to contradict a lot of the Bible, and the books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having sex with women, or Esau being saved, and all kind of wacky things, that is Esau making stuff up to throw you off.

There is a real book of Jasher, and the Pope and them likely have it in the Vatican, in those catacombs. But they put misinformation out there to try to confuse the prophets.

So the chronicles of the kings of Judah and of the kings of Israel, and the book of Jasher, are named in the scriptures but are not in our hands. What is out there under their names is not to be trusted.

precepts.text: The rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon? There is a book called the acts of Solomon, full of the spring of wisdom, things Solomon revealed that the Lord did not want us to know today.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?” So there is a book called the acts of Solomon, and we don't have it today. I would love to read that book.

Some of those books are full of what Ezra was told of the seventy: “For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge.” Things Solomon revealed there, the Lord likely did not want us to know today, so he made it that we don't have possession of those books now.

That is also why the other books out there are left alone: Enoch, Jasher, the letter of Thomas and all that crazy stuff. This is warfare. Evil communication will corrupt you. You go reading that and certain thoughts start coming to your mind, and where did those thoughts come from? From that book you read. If you think you are strong enough to read it, that's on you, but it could confuse you. I'm going to stay with what the Lord gave us.

precepts.text: The rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, are written in the book of the kings of Israel. We do have the prayer of Manasses in the Apocrypha, but that prayer is also part of the book of the kings of Israel, which we do not have.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel.” That is another book, the book of the kings of Israel.

We do have the prayer of Manasseh; it is in the Apocrypha. But that prayer is also part of the book of the kings of Israel, and that book we don't have.

So what are we to do with the books we don't have? Christ answers it in Revelation: “But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.” Today we have 80 books. Don't go looking for other books, and don't try to mix in something someone just found, like a book called Lilith, Adam's second wife. Leave all those books alone.

Read on: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”. If you overcome your lust, the temptations and the white man's lies, and hold on to that little faith and that little understanding you got from these 80 books, you will rule the nations. What is in these 80 books, the laws and the prophecies of what is going to take place, we can get the kingdom with that.

precepts.text: The acts of David the king, first and last, are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer. We have the book of Samuel, but we are missing Nathan and Gad. A seer is a prophet; he sees the future.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer”. We have the book of Samuel, but do we have a book of Nathan the prophet? Do we have a book of Gad the seer? We are missing Nathan and Gad.

Nathan the prophet wrote a book where the Lord showed him certain things. A seer is a prophet: somebody that sees things, sees the future. These look like the books the Lord told Ezra to show only to the wise, because in them are things not everybody can understand.

So we see in part. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face”. The glass we see through darkly is the Bible. God told Moses to hide some things, so we get bits and pieces; one apostle explains it here and another there, and we put together the full picture piece by piece. We don't have all the books, but we have enough to get the understanding to get the kingdom. When Christ comes, he will teach us face to face, and whatever you are confused about now, the Lord will make it clear.

precepts.text: The acts of Solomon are also written in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer. There is a prophet called Ahijah that wrote books we know nothing about. Our forefathers in the time of the Greeks, Judas Maccabeus and the woman with the seven sons, were ready to die because they had a level of understanding from those other books; we are just starting to figure it out piece by piece today.

The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?” Nathan's book is another we are supposed to have. There is also a prophet called Ahijah who wrote books we know nothing about, and Iddo the seer, another prophet, another book.

Those prophets went into some heavy stuff. Ask yourself why, in the time of the Greeks, when Antiochus came against us, Judas Maccabeus, the woman with the seven sons and our forefathers thought the way they did. They were ready to die. Even that group that said, I'd rather die than fight on the Sabbath, just kill me, I'm going to die in my innocency. They had a level of understanding that they got from those seventy books. We are not learning about regeneration and certain things today, but they were far past that back then.

They understood things that we are just starting to figure out piece by piece today. That is why we will never say we understand everything or have one hundred percent truth: “now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” Our flesh cannot contain some of these things, and when Christ returns we will know.

precepts.text: His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him, behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers. There is a book called the sayings of the seers that we do not have today. The Lord took those books away because some things in them we are not to understand today; he wants us to just trust in him.

If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him, and all his sin, and his trespass, and the places wherein he built high places, and set up groves and graven images, before he was humbled: behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers.” So there is a book called the sayings of the seers, the same name as Captain Horab's show, and we don't have it today.

The Lord took those books away. Why? Because some things in them we are not to understand today. He wants us to just trust in him. Some of the things he did back then, he does not want us to have in these last days. And some books were taken away so that the white man could come and lie on the earth and spread all these lies, because some things in those other books were too plain for us to understand. Even though the Vatican took those books and hid them, the Lord allowed that.

One of those missing books is the heart of this class: “Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord”. The Lord there is Christ. He is not only going to war in the future; he has been warring since the beginning. We don't have that book, but we can go into the scriptures and see its record in parts, as here in Joshua 10, where the sun stood still until Israel had avenged themselves upon their enemies.

precepts.text: Abram pursued them unto Dan, yet the land of Dan was not established in Genesis and Israel was not even born yet; proof the scribes leave location markers for the reader.
precepts.point: They feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty. So the five kings of the Amorites, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon, gathered themselves, went up with all their hosts, and made war against Gibeon, because it had made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“Adoni–zedek king of Jerusalem had heard how Joshua had taken Ai”. You might be confused why it says Jerusalem, since Jerusalem had not been set up as of yet because the land was not conquered. When the scribes wrote the history they left identifying location markers, so the reader knows visually where this is taking place.

Genesis proves it: “And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.” Abram pursued them unto Dan, yet the land of Dan was not established in Genesis and Israel was not even born yet. The scribes leave location markers for the reader, and that is why the king of the Amorites is called the king of Jerusalem here.

precepts.text: As in Egypt, the elements themselves were changed to fight against Israel's enemies.
precepts.point: He did the same thing in Egypt: the elements were changed in themselves to fight for Israel, and here he sends down hailstones to destroy the people again.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“the Lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died: they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword.” The Most High was up in heaven aiming the hailstones right at the people, and nobody could escape.

He did the same thing in Egypt: “For the elements were changed in themselves by a kind of harmony, like as in a psaltery notes change the name of the tune, and yet are always sounds; which may well be perceived by the sight of the things that have been done. For earthly things were turned into watery, and the things, that before swam in the water, now went upon the ground. The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own virtue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature.”

As in Egypt, the elements themselves were changed to fight for Israel against her enemies, and here he sends down hailstones from heaven to destroy the people again.

precepts.text: Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no prophecy in it shall fail, and the land is divided to Israel from generation to generation, so the book follows the children of Israel forever.
precepts.point: Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“Is not this written in the book of Jasher?” Why do we not have that book today? “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” The mouth of the Most High commanded and his spirit gathered the books of the Bible for us in these last days. He left the book of Jasher out because we do not need it in this captivity; if he wanted us to read it, he would have left it in the book.

“And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.” No prophecy in it shall fail, and the land is divided to Israel from generation to generation, so the book follows the children of Israel forever. He put the Apocrypha in the 1611 version because he wanted us to read it in the last days; the Protestants and Catholics took it out of the modern Bible in the late 1700s, but you cannot stop the Most High. The Bible will always be with the children of Israel, and no, a white man did not write it: the Most High put it in the hands of our enemies to preserve it. That is the power of God.

Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read. Reading is fundamental. Listening to and watching videos is fine, but nothing takes the place of reading; the hearing of the word strengthens the understanding of what we have read. That is why the leadership set up the four chapters reading, so make sure reading is first and foremost in understanding and applying the words of the Most High.

precepts.point: Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on.

precepts.why:
“And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.” Of making many books there is no end, and much study of books he did not command is a weariness of the flesh.

Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on.

precepts.text: Be not curious in unnecessary matters; think with reverence on what is commanded thee.
precepts.point: Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“Seek not out things that are too hard for thee, neither search the things that are above thy strength. But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret.” Think with reverence on what is commanded thee: the book of the Lord that his spirit gathered, not the book of Jasher he left out.

“Be not curious in unnecessary matters: for more things are shewed unto thee than men understand. For many are deceived by their own vain opinion; and an evil suspicion hath overthrown their judgment.” The book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. More is shewed in the eighty books he gave us than men understand; stay focused on those.

precepts.text: Against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, that ye may know how that the LORD doth put a difference between Egypt and Israel; underline it and put Joshua 10:20-21 next to it.
precepts.point: Christ did not come for all nations; he came for one people. If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.” Underline it and put Joshua 10:20-21 next to it: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Not a dog shall move his tongue against any of the children of Israel, that ye may know the Lord puts a difference between Egypt and Israel. In Joshua, after the very great slaughter, none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel. Those dogs equal nations. The Lord puts a difference between Israel and the nations, in Egypt and in the land of Canaan alike.

If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
Christ called the other nations dogs just as Exodus 11:7 and Joshua 10:21 do: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” And when the woman worshipped him and said, “Lord, help me”, he answered, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.”

Christ did not come for all nations; he came for one people. If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised. The dogs of Exodus, the dogs of Joshua, and the dogs Christ spoke of are the nations, and the Lord put a difference between them and Israel.

precepts.text: Enter into the rock and hide thee in the dust for fear of the LORD; caves are made out of rock, and the day of the LORD is upon everyone that is proud and lofty.
precepts.point: They hid in caves, and that is what the nations are going to do again. What we read in Joshua is future prophecy: in the day of the Most High men shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
The five kings hid in a cave, and that is what the nations are going to do again. “Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty.” Caves are made out of rock. What we read in Joshua is future prophecy.

“The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day. For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low”. The day of the Lord is upon everyone that is proud and lofty, and they shall be brought low, as those kings were brought out of the cave with the feet of the captains of Israel upon their necks.

precepts.text: They shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth; a future prophecy.
precepts.point: They hid in caves, and that is what the nations are going to do again. What we read in Joshua is future prophecy: in the day of the Most High men shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.” In the day of the Most High men shall go into the caves of the earth for fear of the Lord, just as the five kings hid in the cave at Makkedah. A future prophecy.

“In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats; To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.” That is why Joshua said, “Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the Lord do to all your enemies against whom ye fight.” What he did to those five kings he shall do to all the enemies of Israel when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

precepts.text: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, for he that is hanged is accursed of God; they took the kings down so the land would not be defiled.
precepts.point: Everybody that is hung from a tree is cursed. That lets you know all the nations are cursed, and Israel fell up under the curses also.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
Joshua hanged the five kings on five trees until the evening, and at the going down of the sun they took them down. They did it according to the law: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance.”

His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, for he that is hanged is accursed of God. They took the kings down so the land would not be defiled, and cast them into the cave and laid great stones in the cave's mouth.

Everybody that is hung from a tree is cursed. That lets you know all the nations are cursed, and Israel fell up under the curses also.

precepts.text: The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name.
precepts.point: He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
Joshua “utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the Lord God of Israel commanded”, and took all these kings and their land at one time, “because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.” This is why they tell you not to read the Old Testament: the Most High is out there fighting through his people, giving them the spirit to destroy all that breathe, both young and old, leaving none alive.

“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” That is who fought for Israel. A man of war is his name.

precepts.text: Who hath directed the spirit of the LORD, or taught him? The nations are as a drop of a bucket and counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.
precepts.point: He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
Do not think the Most High is unjust in what he does. “Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him? With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?” Nobody taught him or took counsel with him; you cannot show him anything, because he made you and you just got here.

In his infinite wisdom he decreed in his own counsel: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.” The small dust of the balance does not tip the scale at all. “And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.” You could not gather enough wood or sacrifice enough animals to change his mind about the other nations.

“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” All means all: no nation is excluded. No wonder the Most High gave Moses and Joshua the green light to destroy everything that breathed.

precepts.text: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them.
precepts.point: He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.” He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

All the men of Gibeon were mighty, and the kings gathered all their hosts, and Joshua took all these kings and their land at one time because the Lord fought for Israel. The nations are enlarged and then straitened again; that is his doing, and it is not unjust.

If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: The Lord said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee. The Lord was always fighting for us and warring with the nations.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: The Lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them, and they died: they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword. The Lord killed more than we killed. What are we reading? The wars of the Lord.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Joshua said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Time stopped. And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the Lord hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the Lord fought for Israel. The reason it stopped for him is his faith: he believed the Lord would do it.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Is not this written in the book of Jasher? Another record from a book we do not have today.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah, and Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave; stay ye not, but pursue after your enemies. When they brought out those five kings, Joshua called for all the men of Israel and said unto the captains of the men of war, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. And Joshua said unto them, Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the Lord do to all your enemies against whom ye fight. This was Israel conquering the land of Canaan, and it is going to happen again in the future.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: And all these kings and their land did Joshua take at one time, because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Adoni-zedec king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai and utterly destroyed it. You might be confused why it says Jerusalem, since Jerusalem had not been set up as of yet because the land was not conquered: when the scribes wrote the history they left identifying location markers, so the reader knows visually where this is taking place.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: They feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty. So the five kings of the Amorites, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon, gathered themselves, went up with all their hosts, and made war against Gibeon, because it had made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at Gilgal: slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the mountains are gathered together against us.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The LORD said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee. So Joshua ascended from Gilgal all night with all the people of war and the mighty men of valour, and came unto them suddenly.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The LORD discomfited them before Israel, slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the way that goeth up to Beth-horon. As they fled, the LORD cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: They were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword. The Most High was up in heaven aiming the hailstones right at the people, and nobody could escape.
He did the same thing in Egypt: the elements were changed in themselves to fight for Israel, and here he sends down hailstones to destroy the people again.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Joshua spake to the LORD in the sight of Israel: Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. The sun stood still in the midst of heaven and hasted not to go down about a whole day, and there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the LORD fought for Israel.

He put the Apocrypha in the 1611 version because he wanted us to read it in the last days; the Protestants and Catholics took it out of the modern Bible in the late 1700s, but you cannot stop the Most High. The Bible will always be with the children of Israel, and no, a white man did not write it: the Most High put it in the hands of our enemies to preserve it. That is the power of God.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Is not this written in the book of Jasher? Why do we not have that book today? The mouth of the Most High commanded and his spirit gathered the books of the Bible for us in these last days; he left the book of Jasher out because we do not need it in this captivity. If he wanted us to read it, he would have left it in the book.

Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah. Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave, set men by it to keep them, and stay ye not: pursue after your enemies and smite the hindmost of them, for the LORD your God hath delivered them into your hand.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Israel slew them with a very great slaughter till they were consumed, and none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel. Those dogs equal nations.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings unto me: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Joshua called for all the men of Israel and said to the captains of the men of war, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the LORD do to all your enemies against whom ye fight.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: They hid in caves, and that is what the nations are going to do again. What we read in Joshua is future prophecy: in the day of the Most High men shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Afterward Joshua smote them, slew them, and hanged them on five trees until the evening; at the going down of the sun they took them down, cast them into the cave wherein they had been hid, and laid great stones in the cave's mouth, which remain until this very day.
They took them down according to the law: he that is hanged is accursed of God, and the body shall not remain all night upon the tree, that thy land be not defiled.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: That day Joshua took Makkedah and smote it with the edge of the sword; he utterly destroyed all the souls that were therein, he let none remain, and did to the king of Makkedah as he did unto the king of Jericho.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The southern campaign rolled city by city: Libnah, then Lachish, which he took on the second day; Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua smote him and his people until he had left him none remaining.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: From Lachish to Eglon, up to Hebron, and back to Debir: every city taken, its king slain, and all the souls therein utterly destroyed, none remaining, according to all that he had done to the cities before.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: So Joshua smote all the country of the hills, of the south, of the vale, and of the springs, and all their kings; he left none remaining, but utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the LORD God of Israel commanded, from Kadesh-barnea even unto Gaza. All these kings did Joshua take at one time, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.

This is why they tell you not to read the Old Testament: the Most High is out there fighting through his people, giving them the spirit to destroy all that breathe, both young and old, leaving none alive. The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name.

Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering: you could not gather enough wood or sacrifice enough animals to change his mind about the other nations. All nations before him are as nothing, and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity. All means all: no nation is excluded. No wonder the Most High gave Moses and Joshua the green light to destroy everything that breathed.
